overview: The two new DNA strands made during replication, differing in how continuously they can be synthesised given the antiparallel nature of DNA.
genZNote: Leading strand: smooth highway, one continuous drive. Lagging strand: stop-and-go traffic in fragments.

aspects.label: Synthesis Pattern
aspects.valueA: Synthesised continuously in the same direction as the replication fork moves.
aspects.valueB: Synthesised discontinuously, in short Okazaki fragments, away from the fork.

aspects.label: Number of Primers Needed
aspects.valueA: Just one RNA primer to start the whole strand.
aspects.valueB: Multiple RNA primers, one for each Okazaki fragment.

aspects.label: Key Extra Enzyme Involved
aspects.valueB: Requires DNA ligase to join the Okazaki fragments together after primer removal.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Okazaki fragments and the need for DNA ligase are the signature exam clue for the lagging strand.
overlay.memoryTrick: Leading strand leads smoothly. Lagging strand lags behind in fragments.
overlay.commonMisconception: Both strands are synthesised at the same overall rate and at the same time — 'lagging' refers to the fragmented mechanism, not to being slower overall.
